locator.section: 8.2 Product stability (Neutral-product stability; -OH location in hydroxy fatty-acid methyl esters)

evidence.curator_note: Eq 8.17, p.149, step 1 of 2. A hydroxy-substituted fatty-acid methyl ester, drawn as its molecular ion n-ionized at the ESTER carbonyl oxygen: the book prints '+.' on that carbonyl O (map 10), so the precursor SMILES carries =[O+:10] with one radical electron (convention B). 'Analogous' to eq 8.16, the reaction is a hydroxyl-H rearrangement: the carbonyl O radical abstracts the remote hydroxyl H (map 13, on carbinol O map 2) through a large-ring TS, giving the drawn distonic intermediate -- an alkoxy radical on the carbinol O ('.O', map 2) and a protonated ester carbonyl ('H-O+', map 10, now even-electron oxocarbenium). ARC COUNT: the book draws 0 electron arc(s) for this step -- it is denoted only by the 'rH' label over the first arrow (the drawn arcs on the intermediate belong to step 2). The three encoded fishhooks are the balanced H-atom-transfer flow implied by 'rH': move <1> the carbonyl-O odd electron (map 10) into the forming O10-H13 bond; move <2> one electron of the breaking O2-H13 bond into that same forming O10-H13 bond; move <3> the other O2-H13 electron onto oxygen map 2, its new alkoxy radical site. Net: H13 migrates O2 -> O10 and the odd electron migrates O10 -> O2; mass unchanged (still M+.). Instantiated R = CH3, n = 5 (methyl 7-hydroxyoctanoate, M+. = C9H18O3, m/z 174.1250) so the eventual charged fragment is exactly the printed m/z 130 member of the series.

locator.section: 8.2 Product stability (Neutral-product stability; -OH location in hydroxy fatty-acid methyl esters)

evidence.curator_note: Eq 8.17, p.149, step 2 of 2. Radical-site (alpha) cleavage driven by the carbinol alkoxy radical (map 2): the C1-C4 bond alpha to the O radical breaks, the carbinol carbon closes to the aldehyde C1=O2 (neutral R-CHO), and the odd electron is expelled onto the chain carbon (map 4, '.CH2') giving the diagnostic ODD-ELECTRON ester ion. This ion (protonated methyl-ester carbonyl carrying a terminal chain radical) is the OE+. series the text cites at m/z 130, 144, 158, ..., 270 (differing by CH2), which locates the -OH substitution position. ARC COUNT: the book draws 2 arc(s) on the intermediate -- move <1> (the small fishhook off the '.O' radical dot on map 2) = the alkoxy odd electron into the forming C1=O2 pi bond; move <2> (the large curved arc sweeping from the C1-C4 bond up toward the carbinol carbon/oxygen) = one electron of the breaking C1-C4 sigma bond into that same forming C1=O2 pi bond. Move <3>, the other C1-C4 electron onto carbon map 4 (the odd electron of the departing/retained '.CH2' fragment), is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page -- the book simply writes '.(CH2)n' with a radical dot as the product). Instantiated R = CH3, n = 5: neutral = acetaldehyde CH3CHO (C2H4O, not detected); ion = .(CH2)5-C(=O+H)-OCH3 (C7H14O2+., computed monoisotopic m/z 130.0988; the book prints the nominal value 130).

No MOD rule is indexed for eq 8.17 in data/mechanisms/rule_index.json (by_equation has no '8.17' key; checked 2026-07-26). Neither the hydroxyl-H rearrangement (step 1) nor the alkoxy-radical alpha-cleavage (step 2) has a cross-linked Rule.fromDFS encoding, so the electron flow is curator-derived from the printed two-arrow scheme and is NOT verified against any MOD rule.
